verdict.rationale: ReelMimic generates video from what you tell it, but its documented input flow is anchored on a reference video: you drop in a file or link, then describe what you want. A pure text-prompt-to-video path is not evidenced. Iteration without restarting is well documented: you refine the storyboard plan in chat before approving, request changes in chat (screenshots work too), and leave timestamped comments on the finished video that are sent all at once. Missing for 10: evidence of generation from a text prompt alone without a reference video, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the iteration loop.

support.subject: As a creator, I can turn a text prompt into a video clip and iterate on the result without starting from scratch each time

citations.quote: On the home page, drop in a reference video or paste a link, say what you want, and pick Claude Code or Codex.
Chat about it until you like it, then approve.
If you want changes, say so in the chat on the right. Screenshots work too.
When it's done, scrub to any second and type a note. Send them all at once.
